identity.name: neighbourhoods
identity.description: Loads Toronto's 158 Neighbourhood Boundaries (GeoJSON, CRS84) together with the 2021 Neighbourhood Census Profile (XLSX) as a lookup, merging both sources into ONE class-A guarded upsert into neighbourhoods (17 columns + geom) inside a single step-scoped transaction.

why_lock.text: Mutual exclusion with every other writer of neighbourhoods (Spec 47 §A.5 row 57); the shell keeps `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 57;` as a §5.4 source-text constant, asserted equal by the pipeline advisory-lock suite.

why.text: Legacy UNNEST batch INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (neighbourhood_id) DO UPDATE SET with the boundary guard `WHERE neighbourhoods.name IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.name` plus, in the same statement now, the 8 census UPDATEs and the bulk 5-pct arm [READ scripts/load-neighbourhoods.js, anchors `ON CONFLICT (neighbourhood_id) DO UPDATE SET` and `IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.name`]. The census columns carry on_empty preserve_null because legacy keeps the stored value when the source omits one (absent rows keep stored; the bulk arm is literally `COALESCE(v.married_pct, n.married_pct)`), folding 5 autocommit UPDATEs into ONE guarded upsert (N-D2).

Only the guarded upsert writes: the legacy boundary INSERT, the 8 census UPDATEs and the run's VACUUM ANALYZE become one upsert plus a declared execution.maintenance entry [READ scripts/load-neighbourhoods.js, anchors `INSERT INTO neighbourhoods` and `VACUUM ANALYZE neighbourhoods`] (N-D2/N-D9).

N-D4. The legacy probe `SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'postgis'` selected an optional geom SET arm and silently skipped geometry when PostGIS was absent; it is now a fail-loud precondition because geom is a contract column (link-coa-to-parcels reads geometry via Turf and link_neighbourhoods reads n.geom), following the link_neighbourhoods LN-D2 precedent.
Migration 227 enables RLS on neighbourhoods with 0 policies: the upsert works only under rolbypassrls=true, else it affects 0 rows silently while the verdict still reads PASS.

on_row_error_why.text: A feature with no AREA_NAME/AREA_LONG_CODE is skipped and the load continues [READ scripts/load-neighbourhoods.js, anchor `Skipping feature with missing ID or name`], exactly as legacy did. The tolerance is bounded by the FAIL floor `boundaries_loaded`, so a source that degraded into unnamed features cannot pass silently.

on_batch_error_why.text: N-D8. The step owns ONE transaction (txn_scope step), so a failed statement rolls back everything: there is no per-batch boundary left to drop, and legacy's separate boundary/census transactions are retired.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check here reads a counter the library already measured, so a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition — it must redden the run rather than drop its row.

why.text: N-D9. The legacy shell ran `await pool.query('VACUUM ANALYZE neighbourhoods')` on every run, because the full upsert plus census enrichment creates ~1,264 dead tuples on a 158-row table. runMaintenance (EP-D17) now gates it on `neighbourhoods_dead_tuple_ratio_warn_max` and runs it autocommit after the write, exactly as VACUUM requires.

expect.of: rows_shaped (features with a key and a name, pre-dedupe)

why.text: Catastrophic-load detector: the legacy audit row `threshold: '>= 158'` with `status: boundaryCount >= 158 ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'` [READ scripts/load-neighbourhoods.js, anchor `boundaryCount >= 158`]. The bound SHARES the registered variable `sources_neighbourhoods_floor` (default 158) with assert_data_bounds and link_neighbourhoods via limit_from_config — the SAME key, not a second one (Rule 3, one home per concern). The limit uses the R-T addendum `value_min` form, a RAW MEASURED count: pairing `viol == 0` with a FLOOR variable is the AP-D6 trap where resolveLimit substitutes 158 into the flag and compares 0/1 against it.

The legacy INFO audit row `metric: 'census_rows_matched'` [READ scripts/load-neighbourhoods.js], carried so the audit table keeps its row rather than going silent. Purely descriptive (INFO, no negative direction, never gates) and a raw count, so `viol == 0` is the correct limit form with no limit_from_config; N-D10 records that a WARN floor on it is deferred to F2.

expect.violation_when: a feature's AREA_SHORT_CODE is absent, empty or 0

order_guarantee.guarantee: the refusal must land before the write, so neighbourhoods — the FK target of permits and the neighbourhood norms tables — is left untouched, exactly as legacy's abort did.

why.text: N-D6. The dead AREA_S_CD arm and the AREA_ID arm (7-digit ids, which would key 158 wrong rows) are retired, so a key-less feature is now a pre-write refusal rather than a silent skip.

order_guarantee.guarantee: the refusal must land before the write, so neighbourhoods — the FK target of permits and the neighbourhood norms tables — is left untouched, exactly as legacy's abort did.

why.text: N-D7. Legacy aborted with Postgres' `cannot affect row a second time` from its single UNNEST INSERT; the converted dedupe would instead proceed silently, so the refusal is kept here as an explicit pre-write gate.

expect.violation_when: a feature has a null geometry

order_guarantee.guarantee: the refusal must land before the write, so neighbourhoods — the FK target of permits and the neighbourhood norms tables — is left untouched, exactly as legacy's abort did.

why.text: N-D17. Legacy's `ST_GeomFromGeoJSON` of a jsonb 'null' throws and fails the run; the converted parser instead skips and counts such features, so the refusal is kept here.

expect.violation_when: the upsert inserted a NEW boundary row (written.inserted > 0)

why.text: N-D1. The insert path is dead on live input (the 158 rows carry created_at 2026-02-20), and a new City boundary set is a years-scale event, so a NEW boundary row is surfaced rather than treated as routine.

deviations.from: N-D1 — the legacy INSERT `INSERT INTO neighbourhoods (neighbourhood_id, name, geometry)` omits geom, so a NEW row got geom NULL

why.text: Knowingly retired: the insert path is dead on live input (created_at 2026-02-20 on 158/158, 0 NULL geom, no trigger), no schema value can pin an insert-only NULL, and the retired arm would blind link_neighbourhoods' `n.geom IS NOT NULL` corpus; a NEW row is now surfaced by the check boundary_rows_inserted.

deviations.adjudicated_by: Fold CF-4 (Schema-Fidelity/Op-Model seat), Spec 124 §7 LM-D7/A-8 + R-AR.1

deviations.from: N-D2 — 8 unguarded census UPDATEs (`UPDATE neighbourhoods AS n SET`) rewriting 1,264 tuples per unchanged run

why.text: Folded into the guarded upsert with on_empty preserve_null; 2,212/2,212 cells byte-identical (Fold CF-5), so an unchanged rerun writes 0.
Counters now come from written.inserted/updated, so an unchanged source reads 0 updated (158→0) while a real insert reads new.

deviations.from: N-D4 — the PostGIS probe, its optional geom arm and the INFO audit row `has_postgis`

why.text: A DB fact, not a data condition: it is now the fail-loud guard guards.requires postgis, so a missing extension reddens the run instead of silently skipping geometry.

deviations.from: N-D5 — the `data/neighbourhoods-4326.geojson` cache plus the `process.argv[2]`/`[3]` path overrides

why.text: The step downloads from CKAN every run and caches none (cache:"none"), so a stale local file can no longer feed a run; the retired cache was measured byte-identical to CKAN.

deviations.from: N-D6 — the key OR-chain `safeParsePositiveInt(props.AREA_S_CD` (AREA_S_CD ‖ AREA_SHORT_CODE ‖ AREA_ID ‖ '0')

why.text: AREA_S_CD is absent 158/158 (dead) and the AREA_ID arm would key 158 wrong rows; key_property is AREA_SHORT_CODE only, and a key-less feature is now the pre_write FAIL bad_key_count.

deviations.from: N-D7 — the duplicate-key abort `cannot affect row a second time` (one UNNEST INSERT)

why.text: The converted dedupe would proceed silently, so the refusal is retained as the pre_write FAIL duplicate_key_count; 0 duplicates measured.

deviations.from: N-D8 — split transactions (boundary txn + 5 autocommit census UPDATEs + bulk txn)

why.text: Replaced by ONE step-scoped transaction; a partial-census state is unreachable, which is strictly stronger than the legacy arrangement.

deviations.adjudicated_by: address_points Fold B3 / massing M-D11 precedent

deviations.from: N-D9 — `await pool.query('VACUUM ANALYZE neighbourhoods');` on every run

why.text: Now the declared execution.maintenance vacuum_analyze gated on `neighbourhoods_dead_tuple_ratio_warn_max` (EP-D17): the trigger differs (only when dead tuples warrant it) but the effect is data-invisible, since VACUUM changes no row values.
The verdict now derives from the check rows (verdict.js, Rule 10) rather than a hand-threaded boolean; on healthy input both forms read PASS identically.

deviations.from: N-D12 — emitMeta labels `"Census XLSX": ["income", "tenure", "demographics"]` (categories, not fields)

why.text: PIPELINE_META is now derived from the descriptor (external ids plus declared columns) instead of hand-typed category labels, so metadata cannot drift from what the step actually reads and writes.
With geometry_kind polygon, a non-polygon feature is now `skipped_unsupported_type` rather than written; exposure is zero (158/158 MultiPolygon, 0 invalid).

deviations.from: N-D14 — census UPDATEs keyed on every matched id

why.text: A table row whose key is absent from this run's GeoJSON gets no census write, because the upsert only touches primary (GeoJSON-derived) rows; exposure is zero (ids 158/158 equal across GeoJSON, XLSX and DB).

deviations.from: N-D15 — Spec 57 drift (population column, Turf.js, "step 9", NUMERIC incomes)

why.text: Spec 57 is brought as-built (INT incomes, no population column, step 17); the drift was documentary only, with no runtime behavior affected.

deviations.from: N-D17 — null geometry: `ST_GeomFromGeoJSON` of jsonb 'null' throws (UPDATE arm)

why.text: The converted parser skips and counts such features instead of throwing, and the refusal is kept as the pre_write FAIL check `null_geometry_count`; exposure 0/158.

deviations.from: N-D18 — legacy census UPDATE never touched geom

why.text: A census-only change now fires the merged guard and its SET also rewrites `geom = EXCLUDED.geom`, so a geom-drifted row with a census change heals under the converted form only; 0 rows today (derived geom = stored 158/158), pinned wrong-form and fixed post-conversion.

deviations.from: N-D19 — legacy bare `get(url, (response) => {` issued no HEAD

why.text: The converted step HEADs each external, and `on_head_error:"warn_row"` is set on BOTH externals (a WARN head_error row plus proceeding is the closest parity to legacy's unverified fetch).

why.text: Retired: there is no per-byte loop left for a cadence knob to bind to, so the MB-window and duration-string formatting are dropped.

limitations.what: N-D10 — census_rows_matched stays INFO (never verdict-capable) although a floor (31 on the live source) is countable; ④ F2 adds the WARN floor neighbourhoods_census_rows_matched_min.
N-D16 — acquisition has no retry (execution.network.retries 0, legacy parity): a transient CKAN 502 fails the run; ④ F1 adds retries_from_config + backoff.
limitations.measured: cloud run 34769829628 (2026-09-13) halted on an un-retried GET; 0 failed local runs [MEASURED plan §2]

limitations.what: Serial burn — every run consumes ~158 id sequence values (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT evaluates nextval), identical to legacy; id is never projected.

interrupted_why.text: Rule 12 truthful posture. This step is class A (write_discipline.class "guarded_upsert", retract:"none"): it holds NO retraction path and NO scoped delete, and it writes inside ONE step-scoped transaction (execution.txn_scope:"step"). A kill mid-run therefore leaves exactly what that transaction left — either NOTHING (the txn rolled back, no committed rows) or the FULLY-COMMITTED guarded upsert of all 17 columns plus geom; there is no half-cleared neighbourhoods table an incremental gate could misread as complete, and no retraction to recover because none exists. The force_full_on_next_run obligation binds only targets with retract_when full_only or retract:"all" (per the schema's own note on this field) — neither is declared here. Nothing is owed to a successor run beyond re-running the idempotent upsert, which zero-writes on an unchanged source (replay:"idempotent_upsert", idempotent_rerun:"zero_writes"). Genuinely none rather than silently ignored.

before_image_why.text: The generic before-image mechanism (scripts/lib/step/write.js writeBeforeImage) mirrors a retraction's write_discipline.scope predicate as a SELECT — it structurally requires a scope to capture. This step declares retract:"none" with write_discipline.scope:"none", so there is no retraction for the mechanism to mirror and nothing to capture. Every column (the 2 boundary-derived fields, the 8 census characteristics, created_at, census_year and both geometry forms) is re-derived from the sources on every run, so a re-run recovers the same rows identically without a before-image. Declared out of scope rather than silently skipped (parcels' text shape; massing precedent).

why.text: The guarded upsert committed: every parsed feature is inserted or updated (split by RETURNING xmax = 0), with no retraction (retract:"none"). The step has NO staleness gate (staleness.scope:"none"), so success is the NORMAL terminal of every run — an unchanged source is not a skip, it is a zero-writes completed run (idempotent_rerun:"zero_writes").

The declared WARN check tripped with NO FAIL: boundary_rows_inserted is WARN-severity and blocking:false, so a NEW boundary row landing (N-D1) still commits and the run is completed_with_warnings — a new City boundary set is surfaced, never promoted to a halt. The same terminal carries a WARN head_error row from either external (on_head_error:"warn_row", N-D19), which lists as a warning row and proceeds rather than failing the run.

boundaries_loaded fell below sources_neighbourhoods_floor (default 158) — the legacy audit row `threshold: '>= 158'` flipped to FAIL. The FAIL row is declared; blocking:false, so the run reads as failed and the chain continues (the load already committed exactly as the legacy loader wrote its FAIL row and exited 0).

bad_key_count, duplicate_key_count or null_geometry_count FAILed at the pre_write gate: NO transaction was opened, so neighbourhoods — the FK target of permits and the neighbourhood norms tables — is untouched, exactly as legacy's abort on duplicates (`cannot affect row a second time`) or null geometry did (N-D6/N-D7/N-D17).

A download of either external (the GeoJSON boundaries or the census XLSX), the GeoJSON/XLSX parse, or coerceKey on a non-numeric AREA_SHORT_CODE threw before any write was attempted; legacy halted on the same conditions (its `/positive integer/` key check threw too). neighbourhoods is untouched (no transaction was opened).
inputs.expect_nonempty is true: a source that shapes to ZERO features fails rather than landing an empty 'success' — an empty boundaries file is a publisher error, not an empty load.

Advisory lock 57 is held by another process. Pre-conversion the step returned silently when the lock was not acquired (legacy `if (!lockResult.acquired) return;`); the library now emits a row-derived WARN summary instead of a silent return.
